objective: Test whether a loop's presence can be computed from the loop's own structure instead of declared, so that two loops bound by an atom satisfy K1-K3 on the computed presences with no outside input and a presentation-independent verdict. Candidates: self-supporting cycles in static semantics and recurrences of a deterministic update. If every candidate collapses to a free bit, needs an outside input, or depends on how the system is split into parts, record that presence is primitive.
status: Retired on 2026-10-19: under the forgetting reading a loop's presence is not a variable, so the question of where presence comes from no longer arises; a loop is a structure with an open distinction (docs/KNOT_INTUITION.md). The exploratory pass stays in research/KNOT-FOUNDATION-20261019-001/presence.md.
title: Where a loop's presence comes from
